contract_worst_attestation_estimate.name: Contract worst-case P7 attestation round trip (ESTIMATE)
contract_worst_attestation_estimate.formula: KDF ~100 + CHALLENGE MAC <=269 + transport ~30 + endpoint ~600 + RESPONSE MAC <=792 + transport ~40 + RESPONSE verify <=792 + tag check ~100
contract_worst_attestation_estimate.notes: Stated as 'about 2,700 cycles, ESTIMATE' in the signed contract. Not a measurement. Includes the Q-class bound (792) twice.

hold_interval_event_boundary.end: GRANT delivered at tile 3 (trusted completion; n2p7_rtt: GRANT HEAD into mesh -> delivered at tile 3)

service_path_event_boundary.begin: app_ready[3] rises and the CPU request is accepted by the NI (after endpoint releases the port)

justification: M-F1 rev 8 Sec. 3 Rule 6: app_ready[3] = 0 while the endpoint owns the port; the CPU request cannot be accepted by the NI while app_ready[3] = 0.
M-F1 rev 8 Sec. 5 defines the worst legitimate wait as: port hold + NI store-and-forward + mesh round trip + front-end service (additive by contract).
The I-5 hold interval contains only attestation traffic (CHALLENGE/RESPONSE/GRANT); no CPU memory request NI/mesh/memory service lies inside it.
unverified_assumptions: The exact RTL cycle at which app_ready[3] rises is not a registered measurement; it is taken as the GRANT-delivered boundary. If it rises earlier the true wait is smaller (conservative).
The hold is assumed to begin no earlier than attestation start. A hold beginning earlier would add cycles not captured by the measurement.
The 3-cycle NI store-and-forward, 2-cycle front-end and 1-cycle egress allowances are ANALYTICAL_ASSUMPTION, not registered measurements.
Only the NONE and LOADED conditions were measured (4 attestations each). Heavier loads are not covered by measurement.

model_input_selection.reason: Step 12 computes the worst legitimate CPU wait for D7, so the largest registered measurement is used. 1,204 is the unloaded condition and is retained only as a labelled reference.

arbiter_applicability.provenance: M-F1 R7.6 (frozen), bench-checked by I-5 assertion A3 (every job <= J_MAX)
arbiter_applicability.applies_to: Each L2 KMAC job inside the attestation hold
arbiter_applicability.rationale: Per-job duration is already inside the measured 1,204/1,206-cycle hold and inside the P and Q bounds, which are conditional on J_MAX. Adding it separately would double count.

arbiter_applicability.provenance: M-F1 R7.6a (re-frozen 2026-10-20: P <= 269 for J_MAX=128, OVH<=4); exhaustive arbiter model
arbiter_applicability.applies_to: RoT-class requesters r0 (tile-4 TX: CHALLENGE, GRANT, REVOKE) and r1 (tile-3 RX of the reserved peer slot)
arbiter_applicability.rationale: Applied once, as a conservative single-wait increment on the attestation hold (scenario contention_wait_arbiter_p). It is not a complete worst-case hold: that is covered by the contract-estimate scenario.

arbiter_applicability.provenance: M-F1 R7.6a (re-frozen: Q <= 792); starvation test checks Q <= 792
arbiter_applicability.applies_to: Non-RoT requesters r2 (tile-3 TX: RESPONSE) and r3 (tile-4 RX: RESPONSE verify); both lie inside the attestation hold
arbiter_applicability.rationale: Q affects how long the attestation hold can last under contention, not the CPU request itself. It is not added to the P scenario; it enters only through the contract-estimate scenario (RESPONSE MAC <= 792 and RESPONSE verify <= 792).

arbiter_applicability.provenance: I5_GATE_20261029.md hop table ('7 (data plain in P7)' for VC0 MEM_WR_REQ) and L2 verdict row (CHALLENGE / RESPONSE / GRANT / REVOKE only)
arbiter_applicability.rationale: Data-plane packets are plain in P7 and do not use the shared L2 KMAC engine, so no P/Q/J arbitration is traversed by the request. Conclusion rests on the I-5 report and contract text, not on RTL inspection by Engineer 4.

arbiter_applicability.applies_to: Revocation transient stacked onto the wait
arbiter_applicability.rationale: Stacked conservatively on top of the attestation hold. It is an upper-bound construction, not an observed combined event.

timeout_evaluation.justification: A 4,096-cycle bridge timeout (PROPOSED, not approved) exceeds every modelled legitimate wait: 1234 nominal (loaded-max hold), 1503 with one P wait, 1720 with C4 max, 2728 at the contract ESTIMATE and 2734 at the stacked C4 bound. Margins: 2.38x over C4 max, 1.50x over the stacked bound, 1.50x over the contract estimate, and it stays 24.4x below VERIFIER_TIMEOUT. Pending Kalash approval per contract D7.

scenario_1_nominal_arrival.description: Nominal response at cycle 118 (<600) completes cleanly.

scenario_2_boundary_arrival.description: Response at cycle 599 immediately before 600-cycle threshold completes.

scenario_3_response_after_timeout.description: Response at cycle 605 (>600) is safely dropped.

scenario_4_missing_response_release.description: Missing response releases slot autonomously at cycle 600.

scenario_5_slot_reallocation.description: Slot immediately reallocated after timeout release.

scenario_6_late_response_dropped.description: Late response arriving into empty slot is dropped safely.

scenario_7_stale_response_mismatch.description: Stale response for previous tag 0x70 dropped; active tag 0x71 untouched.

scenario_8_reset_cleanup.description: Hardware reset immediately releases both occupied slots.

scenario_9_busy_retry_exhaustion.description: BUSY retries permitted for 0..3 attempts; 4th fails closed.
